Ambuj Nath
For the Appellant : Mr. R. S. Mazumdar, Sr. Advocate For the Respondent : Mr. Pankaj Kumar, P.P.

For the Informant : Mr. Anil Kr. Sinha, Advocate ---------
I.A.(Cr.) No. 1350 of 2023 03/20.02.2023 Heard Mr. R. S. Mazumdar, learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, Mr. Pankaj Kumar, learned P.P. for the State assisted by Mr. Anil Kr.
Sinha, learned counsel appearing for the informant.
The instant interlocutory application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Sections 366A/376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 6 of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for twenty years along with a fine of Rs. 20,000/- for the offence under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
The sister of the informant was alleged to have been enticed away by the appellant.
The victim was recovered subsequently and has been examined as P.W. - 1 in course of trial and the tenor of her evidence reveals a love affair existing between the appellant and the victim.

The age of the victim as per the witnesses was 17 years at the time of the incident.

sentences.text: Regard being had to the evidence of P.W. - 1, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during the pendency of this appeal, the appellant, named above, is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Special Judge, Bokaro, in connection with Special POCSO Case No. 50 of 2022 arising out of Chandrapura P. S. Case No. 50 of 2022.
I.A.(Cr.) No. 1350 of 2023 stands allowed and disposed of.
